This work serves as a companion to their previous publication, which highlighted prominent women, and it explores the lives and personalities of notable courtiers, poets, and wits primarily from the Restoration and the following centuries. The Whartons aim to entertain rather than offer a dry historical account, making these essays accessible and engaging for readers interested in the vibrant personalities of the past. The narrative dives into the context of the Restoration of Charles II, using Samuel Pepys as a lens to view the excitement of the time. Villiers's life unfolds as a tale of adventure, loyalty, and wit, marked by his connections to the royal family and his indomitable spirit. The opening offers insight into Buckingham's character, hinting at his charm and tumultuous relationships, while setting the stage for a deeper exploration of the lives of other notable 'wits' and 'beaux' in 17th-century society.
